Perfect! The regex has been successfully created and tested. Here's what the regex does:

## Regex Pattern Breakdown:

**`^(?=.*\b(?:0|[1-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\.(?:0|[1-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\.(?:0|[1-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\.(?:0|[1-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\b)`** - Lookahead ensuring an IPv4 address exists on the line

**`.*(\b\d{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])\b)`** - Captures a YYYY-MM-DD date with proper word boundaries

**`(?!.*\b\d{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])\b).*$`** - Negative lookahead ensuring no more dates after the captured one (ensures it's the LAST date)

## Key Features:
- ✅ **IPv4 Validation**: Matches 0-255 with no leading zeros (octet pattern: `(?:0|[1-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])`)
- ✅ **Date Format**: YYYY-MM-DD with months 01-12 and days 01-31 (Feb 29 allowed for all years)
- ✅ **Word Boundaries**: `\b` ensures dates/IPs aren't preceded/followed by alphanumeric characters
- ✅ **Last Date Only**: Negative lookahead prevents matching if another date exists after it on the same line
- ✅ **Requires IPv4**: Lookahead ensures the line contains an IPv4 address

The regex is saved in `/app/regex.txt` and ready to use with Python's `re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE)`.
